title: Planar fill sampling flips whole curved-boundary faces: inscribed 6-chord region polys + boundary-biased faceInteriorPoint drop round-brush crescents/cracks (straight-edge/square-nib inputs immune)
description:
AUDIT (round-nib visual bugs; square nib used as correctness oracle). Fill-region CLASSIFICATION flips ENTIRE faces of the brush ribbon when the face is bounded by quadratic arcs — the round-nib brush is the canonical producer; straight-edge inputs (the square nib, rects) are exactly immune, which is why the square brush is flawless on identical strokes. This is NOT an arrangement-topology bug: the repro below has a fully valid arrangement (no missed crossings); the defect is purely in how a face's fill is DECIDED.

MECHANISM (two co-factors, both in shared sampling code, both only harmful for CURVED boundaries):
1. `chordPolygon` in packages/core/src/engine/planar/build.ts:298-311 flattens each fill-region quadratic into just 6 chords, INSCRIBED in the curve. Region membership in `assignFaceFillsBySampling` (build.ts:203-241) is then `pointInPolygon` against these inscribed polys — so every curved region has a sagitta BAND (up to ~0.12px for a nib-size quarter-arc; up to ~0.6px beyond the true circle for the current corner-control disk arcs) that reads as OUTSIDE the region even though it is inside the actual curve.
2. `faceInteriorPoint` (packages/core/src/engine/planar/query.ts:74-138) tries the boundary-VERTEX-AVERAGE first, with FACE_SAMPLES=16 points per curved half-edge REGARDLESS of edge length (query.ts:22,42-51) — so tiny curve fragments near intersections weight the average toward the curved boundary. The chosen interior point of a FAT face frequently lands within the sagitta band of co-factor 1.
Combined: one point sample in the band -> the ENTIRE face (hundreds of px^2) is assigned fill=null (or, symmetrically, a wrong fill) — catastrophic amplification of a sub-0.1px approximation error.

HARD EVIDENCE (round vs square, identical input):
- 2-sample round stroke (30,30)->(34,33), half=12 (a realistic short dab / stroke end): the arrangement is topologically valid, yet the crescent face of disk B not covered by disk A — face area 124.34px^2 — is classified fill=null. Its faceInteriorPoint = (42.15,23.35): distance from disk B centre = 12.631 (INSIDE B's actual boundary arc, which reaches 12.728 there) but OUTSIDE the 6-chord inscribed polys of BOTH disks (verified: pointInPolygon false for both). Committed result (foldShapeIntoLayer -> renderer-faithful nonzero raster): ~391 half-px grid points (~98px^2, a quarter of the visible dab crescent) UNPAINTED. Square nib, same samples: 0 defects.
- Self-overlap loop spine [(20,50),(40,48),(60,47),(80,49),(100,50),(102,30),(100,12),(80,10),(62,12),(60,30),(60,50),(60,70),(61,90)] at DENSE spacing 3px, half=8 (slow careful stroke; disks overlap heavily): 1021 interior points unpainted (cracks in the band near the crossing and along the closing overlap). Square: 0. At spacing 5/8: 1233/1498 (half=4, the DEFAULT brush size 8, fails too). The remaining defects on SPARSE strokes also involve the sibling brushpaint.ts tangent-seam task; this task owns the dense-spacing + dab-crescent failures, which classification alone explains.

WHY EXACTNESS IS THE RIGHT FIX: when the arrangement is valid, every face lies entirely inside or entirely outside each source region — so an EXACT membership test is correct for ANY interior point, killing the band entirely and making the single-point-per-face design sound. (When topology is broken — sibling task — no sampler can be right; both tasks are needed for full square-parity.)

SUGGESTED FIX:
1. Replace the inscribed 6-chord membership test with an EXACT curve-aware point-in-region test for the fill regions: even-odd/winding via ray-quadratic intersection (solving one quadratic per curved segment per ray — cheap, closed-form; mirror edgeBBox's per-axis quadratic handling). Keep the polygon path for straight segments. Regions are built once per fold in buildArrangementFromShapes (build.ts:97-136 fillRegions) — store the segment geometry (EdgeGeometry list), not a pre-flattened poly.
   - Fallback option (weaker, but bounded): adaptive flattening with guaranteed sagitta <= 0.5 twip (0.025px) instead of fixed 6 chords, PLUS nudge: classify with 3 jittered samples and majority-vote. Must still pass acceptance.
2. De-bias `faceInteriorPoint`: sample curved half-edges proportionally to arc length (or cap total samples per edge relative to length) so micro-fragments cannot dominate the vertex average; prefer the max-clearance grid candidate over the first hit when the centroid fails. (Secondary hardening — the exact test in (1) is the primary fix.)
3. Audit the OTHER inscribed-chord consumers for the same band error where it changes behavior: shapeChordPolys/pointInShapeFill in brushpaint.ts:96-125 (brush paint-mode clipping guard), consumeStrokesUnderFills (build.ts:166-191, stroke midpoints within the band of a covering fill), locateFace/pointInFace flattening in query.ts. Fix where reachable, or document why not.

ACCEPTANCE:
- New unit test: the 2-sample dab repro paints the FULL crescent — renderer-faithful raster of the committed shape has ZERO unpainted points with dist(pt,spine) <= half-0.35 (0.5px grid), matching the square nib's zero on its Chebyshev footprint.
- Dense-loop repro (spacing 3, half=8 and half=4): zero unpainted interior points.
- No face whose interior point lies inside the TRUE curved region may classify null: add a direct regression asserting face 'crescent' fill != null for the dab arrangement.
- Existing gates stay green: brush-ribbon.test.ts, planar.test.ts, planar-merge.test.ts, eraser tests, merge-drawing-oracle e2e (fill sampling is shared — run the full core suite).

Files: packages/core/src/engine/planar/build.ts (chordPolygon, assignFaceFillsBySampling, fillRegions), packages/core/src/engine/planar/query.ts (faceInteriorPoint, FACE_SAMPLES), possibly brushpaint.ts:96-125 (audit item 3 only). Parallelizable with the sibling brushpaint.ts geometry task (disjoint primary files); full square-parity on sparse self-overlap strokes requires both.
